chapter_title: [C]oncerning the Father of Gr[eat]ness: [ho]w he i
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

---

**¶2:** Immeasurably great is the [GAP-1: divine kingdom of] wisdom in the perception of those who will receive and acknowledge it, by virtue of the inmost Divine Love itself. How the Divine exists and is established in His five essential faculties of wisdom, which are [GAP-2: the infinite receptacle]-forms of good and truth that have neither boundary nor end to the[GAP-3: ir capacity —] understanding, intellection, interior perception, deliberation of will, and [GAP-4: reflective discernment —] His twelve essential faculties of wisdom that are His twelve plenitudes of divine truth in complete fullness.

---

**¶3:** Now, there are five essential faculties of wisdom within each single one, [GAP-5: and from each] five great [GAP-6: inexhaustible] sources of truth well up and flow forth — [GAP-7: five great] processions of [GAP-8: divine wisdom flowing outward from the Divine.]

---

**¶4:** The first is His wisdom that illum[GAP-9: inates all understanding;] it proceeded forth from Him and pour[GAP-10: ed into] all heavenly states.

---

**¶5:** The second is the perception of Divine [GAP-11: good, which emanates from Him] and pervades all the heavenly states of the Divine itself.

---

**¶6:** The third is His living proceeding truth of [GAP-12: the Divine Word, which fills] all His heavenly states [GAP-13: with its influx.]

---

**¶7:** The fourth is His [GAP-14: blessèd]-ness — [GAP-15: the delight of Divine love that] proceeds from Him [GAP-16: and flows] out [GAP-17: into all who receive it.]

---

**¶8:** The fif[th] is His great glori[GAP-18: ous form of Divine order] that [GAP-19: has always existed, and w]hich has been manifested through all states, whi[ch contin]ues [GAP-20: to permeate] all of them. It was inscribed upon their interiors [GAP-21: and] confirmed in the[GAP-22: ir inmost will,] sealed [GAP-23: into their understanding,] as they transmit [GAP-24: this influx onward] in [GAP-25: reciprocal communion, and] they too receive spiritual sustenance [GAP-26: from the Divine,] immediately [GAP-27: renewed through His] living proceeding trut[GAP-28: h, which fills them with] heavenly delight [GAP-29: and causes all things to be] established anew. It shall proceed forth from within them [GAP-30: to those below, and] they shall [GAP-31: be filled with goods and truths] and become enriched in the [GAP-32: fullness of wisdom. This] too is the beauty of spiritual form [GAP-33: — the very] image [GAP-34: of the Divine] clothed in external truths [GAP-35: of order,] and they live [GAP-36: in this state of reception from the Divine] forever.

---

### Note on the structure

The five faculties that proceed from the Divine correspond to a graduated descent of influx: **(1)** wisdom illuminating the understanding, **(2)** perception of good penetrating the will, **(3)** living truth as the proceeding Word, **(4)** blessedness or spiritual delight flowing from love, and **(5)** the total Divine form or order that contains and confirms all four prior faculties within the receiving vessels. The twelvefold wisdom signifies completeness — all truths of faith in their fullness. The repeated image of "gushing forth" is the correspondence for *proceeding* — the continuous outflowing of life from the Divine into created states, which then reciprocally receive, are nourished, and transmit that life further: the very pulse of influx and reception that Swedenborg calls the universal law of spiritual life.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Very great is [land of] light in the presence of they who will hear and know it, due to the first Father of Greatness. How he ex[ists and is] established in his five light limbs, which are [like the store]houses that have neither limit nor measure to the[m, which are] mind, thought, insight, counsel and [consideration. And] his twelve light limbs that are his twelve wisdoms.
Now, there are five great light lim[bs] in each one [of them, and] five grea[t] springs of praise gush for[th. And] five great [rivers of] lig[ht that flow from him]
The first is his light that enlig[htens all things] it gushed forth from him and pour[ed into] a[l] aeons.
The second is the perfume of the [Father that gushes from him] and pervades all the aeons of greatness.
The third is his living voice of [joy that gushes from him and fills] all his aeons [with praise]
The fourth is his [sweet]-ness [that] gushes forth from him [and flows o]ut [into all the aeons]

The fif[th] is his great glorio[us form] that [has always existed, w]hich [has been ma]nifested all the tim[e], whi[ch contin]ues [in] all of them. It was sculpted in them [and] sealed in the [mind, and] sealed [in the thought] as they send [it forth] in [praise to one another, and] they too receive nourishment [from him] immediately [renewed through his] living voi[ce. It fills them with] joy [and all things are] set up anew. It shall gush forth from it [to those beneath, and] they shall [be filled] and become rich in the [light. This] too is beautiful [in its] portray[al of him, the] adornment [of beauty] and they live [in the light of the Father] for ev[e]r.

fills.explanation: "Land of light" is the standard Manichaean Kephalaia phrase for the divine realm; the spiritual reading's "divine kingdom of" is simply its spiritual sense, confirming the editor's choice.
The five light limbs are compared to storehouses (receptacle-forms) without limit; "like" is the standard Kephalaia comparison introducing the simile.
Completes "them" and introduces the five faculties by name; the spiritual reading's "capacity —" indicates an identifying clause listing the five limbs.
Completes the fifth faculty "consideration" (reflective discernment) and transitions with "And" to the twelve wisdoms, following the paragraph's structure of listing both five and twelve attributes.
Specifies "in each one of them" (each of the twelve wisdoms contains five limbs) and connects with "and" to the springs that gush forth, matching the spiritual reading's "and from each."
Completes "gush forth" and transitions to the second parallel description of five rivers of light, following the structural pattern of paired emanation descriptions.
Rivers of light are standard Manichaean imagery for divine processions flowing outward; parallels the "springs of praise" in the preceding clause.
Completes "light" and describes the rivers flowing from the Father, corresponding to the spiritual sense of divine wisdom proceeding outward from the Divine.
Completes "enlightens all things" — the first attribute (light/sight) illuminates everything, corresponding to wisdom illuminating all understanding.
Completes "poured into" — the standard Kephalaia verb for influx flowing into the aeons, matching the proceeding of divine life.
The perfume (fragrance) emanates from the Father; follows the parallel pattern of ¶4 where each attribute is named, sourced, and described as flowing forth.

fills.fill: joy that gushes from him and fills
fills.explanation: Follows the pattern of ¶4–5 where each attribute has a quality, issues from the Father, and pervades the aeons; the living voice corresponds to proceeding truth which fills all heavenly states.

The voice fills the aeons with praise, completing the pattern where each attribute pervades or fills the aeons with its specific quality; praise is the natural-plane term for spiritual influx through truth.
The fourth of the five sensory attributes of the Father of Greatness is always "sweetness" (taste) in standard Manichaean cosmology, corresponding to spiritual blessedness/delight in Swedenborg.
Simple relative pronoun connecting the attribute to its verb, following the same pattern as ¶4 ("his light that enlightens") and ¶5 ("perfume...that gushes").
Completes "and flows out" — the sweetness gushes forth and flows outward, matching the spiritual sense of divine delight proceeding from love.
The sweetness flows out into all the aeons, following the pattern where each attribute pervades all heavenly states.
Completes "glorious form" — the fifth attribute is form/beauty (εἶδος) in standard Manichaean cosmology, the total Divine order containing all prior attributes.
The divine form has always existed (is eternal), completing the clause before "which has been manifested," expressing the eternal nature of Divine order.
The divine form continues "in" all of them — expressing permeation of Divine order through all receiving states.
Simple conjunction connecting the parallel actions: "sculpted in them AND sealed in the mind," expressing inscription upon the interiors followed by confirmation.
"Mind" (starting with m) corresponds to the inmost will/volitional faculty in the Kephalaia's own terminology; "and" connects to the parallel sealing in the thought (understanding).
Parallel to "sealed in the mind" — the divine form is sealed in both mind (will) and thought (understanding), the two fundamental receiving faculties in Swedenborg's framework.
The aeons "send it forth" — transmitting the received influx onward, expressing the universal law of reception and transmission of divine life.

The aeons send forth praise to one another in reciprocal communion — the Kephalaia's natural-plane image for the mutual exchange and reciprocal influx that Swedenborg describes as the pulse of spiritual life.
The aeons receive nourishment "from him" (the Father/Divine source), expressing reception of spiritual sustenance from the Divine.
The aeons are immediately "renewed through his" living voice — expressing spiritual renewal through the proceeding truth of the Divine Word.
Completes "voice" and begins a new clause describing how the living voice fills the aeons with joy, expressing the influx of truth producing heavenly delight.
The joy from the divine voice causes all things to be "set up anew" — expressing how influx of truth establishes and renews all spiritual states.
The divine life gushes forth to those in lower states, expressing the descending flow of influx from higher to lower, and transitioning to the next clause.
Those below "shall be filled" with goods and truths, then "become rich" — expressing the progressive reception of divine influx.
"Light" is the Kephalaia's natural term for divine wisdom/truth; "This" begins a new sentence describing the beauty of the divine form, matching the spiritual reading's "fullness of wisdom. This."
Connects "beautiful" to "portrayal" — the divine form is beautiful "in its" portrayal, expressing how spiritual beauty manifests in its visible image.
Completes "portrayal of him" (portrayal of the Divine) and introduces "the adornment" as a parallel description, matching the spiritual reading's "image of the Divine clothed in external truths."
The "adornment of beauty" corresponds to the spiritual sense of external truths of order — beauty being the natural-plane correspondence for divine order in Swedenborg.

fills.fill: in the light of the Father
fills.explanation: The aeons live eternally "in the light of the Father" — expressing the state of perpetual reception from the Divine, the Kephalaia's standard image for dwelling in divine wisdom forever.
